entry.title: Unified Convergence Theory of Stochastic and Variance-Reduced Cubic Newton Methods
entry.summary: We study stochastic Cubic Newton methods for solving general possibly non-convex minimization problems. We propose a new framework, which we call the helper framework, that provides a unified view of the stochastic and variance-reduced second-order algorithms equipped with global complexity guarantees. It can also be applied to learning with auxiliary information. Our helper framework offers the algorithm designer high flexibility for constructing and analyzing the stochastic Cubic Newton methods, allowing arbitrary size batches, and the use of noisy and possibly biased estimates of the gradients and Hessians, incorporating both the variance reduction and the lazy Hessian updates. We recover the best-known complexities for the stochastic and variance-reduced Cubic Newton, under weak assumptions on the noise. A direct consequence of our theory is the new lazy stochastic second-order method, which significantly improves the arithmetic complexity for large dimension problems. We also establish complexity bounds for the classes of gradient-dominated objectives, that include convex and strongly convex problems. For Auxiliary Learning, we show that using a helper (auxiliary function) can outperform training alone if a given similarity measure is small.
entry.arxiv:comment: Published in Transactions on Machine Learning Research

entry.title: RanSOM: Second-Order Momentum with Randomized Scaling for Constrained and Unconstrained Optimization
entry.summary: Second-order momentum corrects the lag of momentum behind the current gradient with a Hessian-vector product (HVP), but existing corrections need either a Lipschitz Hessian or extra forward and backward passes at an auxiliary point. We show that randomizing the step length removes this trade-off: if the step is exponentially distributed with mean $η$, a Stein-type identity makes $η$ times one HVP at the new iterate an estimate of the gradient change that is unbiased in expectation over the step, and this HVP shares its forward pass with the next gradient. The resulting method, RanSOM-E, works with normalized, sign, and Muon-type steps, and a Beta-distributed variant, RanSOM-B, keeps Frank-Wolfe iterates feasible. For objectives with Lipschitz gradient and heavy-tailed gradient and Hessian noise with tail indices $p, q \in (1,2]$, RanSOM-E attains the optimal oracle-complexity exponents for every pair $(p,q)$, including $p \neq q$, without a Lipschitz Hessian or clipping ($\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-3})$ for $p = q = 2$). On CIFAR-10 with ResNet-20, we detect no accuracy difference from existing second-order momentum methods, and its mean update time is lower than that of the auxiliary-point method.

entry.title: Stochastic Compositional Optimization via Hybrid Momentum Frank--Wolfe
entry.summary: Stochastic compositional optimization minimizes $F(f(x), x)$ over a compact convex set when the inner map $f$ is available only through noisy samples. We propose Hybrid Momentum Stochastic Frank--Wolfe, a projection-free method for outer functions $F$ that are jointly convex and Lipschitz but not necessarily differentiable, such as maxima, CVaR, and norms. The method tracks the Jacobian and the value of $f$ with momentum, using a Taylor correction for the value, and passes the tracked linearization to a generalized linear minimization oracle. Under finite-variance noise, it attains an expected generalized Frank--Wolfe gap of order $K^{-1/4}$ for non-convex objectives and, when the linearized models minorize the objective, a last-iterate primal error of order $K^{-1/3}$. The analysis extends to heavy-tailed noise without clipping, with separate moment orders for values and Jacobians. With an exact oracle, the method reduces to the deterministic method of Vladarean et al. (2023).

entry.title: Fixed-Time ISS for Interconnected Discrete-Time Systems, Part II: Finite-Horizon Lyapunov Functions
entry.summary: We study fixed-time input-to-state stability (FxT-ISS) for discrete-time systems subject to exogenous inputs using finite-horizon Lyapunov functions. In the proposed Lyapunov- based characterization, the effect of the initial condition is eliminated after a uniformly bounded number of iterations. This characterization encompasses existing extinction-based Lyapunov conditions while allowing more general finite-memory mechanisms. Building on this framework, we establish a finite-horizon small-gain theorem for interconnected discrete-time systems, providing conditions under which FxT-ISS is preserved under feedback interconnections. The proposed framework is illustrated through examples arising in distributed algorithms, optimization, and feedback optimization.

entry.title: SURF: Steering the Scalarization Weight to Uniformly Traverse the Pareto Front
entry.summary: Scalarization is widely used in multi-objective optimization owing to its simplicity and scalability. In many applications, the goal is to generate solutions that represent diverse user preferences, ideally with uniform coverage of the Pareto front (PF). However, uniformly sampling scalarization weights usually induces non-uniform coverage of the PF. We explain this mismatch through the geometry of the scalarization path. As the weight varies, the corresponding solutions traverse the PF at a generally nonuniform speed. Integrating this speed gives cumulative arc length. After normalization by the total length, it defines a cumulative distribution function (CDF) on weights whose inverse selects points at equal arc-length intervals. Building on this insight, we propose SURF (Sampling Uniformly along the Pareto Front). For structured problems, including bi-objective bandits, we derive analytical expressions for this CDF map and the resulting PF-aware weight sampling rule. For general problems, SURF alternates between CDF reconstruction and weight sampling. Theoretically, we show that under provable conditions for bi-objective LS, SURF's CDF reconstruction error converges linearly to an $O(N^{-2})$ discretization floor. Empirically, experiments on bandits, multi-objective-gymnasium, and multi-objective LLM alignment demonstrate that SURF efficiently achieves more uniform PF coverage than baselines.

entry.title: Second-Order Optimization with Asynchronous Curvature
entry.summary: Second-order methods make fast progress per iteration, but forming and factorizing the Hessian often dominates their wall-clock time. We study \emph{Split-Client}, a task-parallel design in which a curvature client factorizes Hessians in the background while a gradient client takes cubic-regularized steps with the most recently published matrix, so that curvature cost appears as a delay rather than as blocking time. For delayed exact Hessians, we prove a first-order stationarity bound that depends on the average age of the curvature rather than its maximum, using an overlap count and a weighted Hardy inequality that allows any bounded-error initial matrix; the analysis extends to subsampled and uniformly inexact curvature. Under a fixed-cost model, the resulting wall-clock bound matches the scaling of optimally tuned Lazy Hessian without choosing a reuse period. In experiments on two LIBSVM datasets, an implementation decreases the objective earlier in wall-clock time than Lazy and Vanilla cubic Newton, with the largest gains at intermediate accuracy.
entry.arxiv:comment: Old title: A Split-Client Approach to Second-Order Optimization

entry.title: PLUTO: An Agentic AI Tool for Interactive Spacecraft Rendezvous Trajectory Design
entry.summary: Modern space missions require trajectory design methods capable of efficiently adapting to diverse mission objectives and operational constraints. Despite the maturity of non-convex trajectory optimization techniques, their broader adoption remains limited by the substantial domain expertise required to tailor problem formulations across varying mission scenarios. Recent advances in large language model (LLM) reasoning and agentic AI coding capabilities offer a promising pathway to improving the accessibility of advanced trajectory optimization techniques. This paper introduces PLUTO (Plain Language Understanding for Trajectory Optimization), an interactive trajectory design framework that integrates agentic AI coding tools within a sequential convex programming (SCP) architecture. The proposed system maps high-level semantic inputs to well-defined mathematical constraints while preserving a structured representation suitable for SCP. These constraints are processed through an auto-convexification pipeline and incorporated directly into executable optimal control formulations, thereby systematically connecting user intent and trajectory generation. Visual constraint verification and scenario parameterization further support an intuitive environment for trajectory design across a wide range of application scenarios. Within an evaluation of 50 natural-language rendezvous mission prompts spanning 10 constraint types, PLUTO generated a trajectory for every prompt, and 94% of the resulting trajectories satisfied both the quantitative and qualitative requirements of the mission intent. Ultimately, this work explores the potential of agentic AI to bridge the gap between advanced optimization algorithms and engineer-focused trajectory design workflows.
entry.arxiv:comment: 10 pages, 4 figures, 2 tables. Submitted to the 2027 IEEE Aerospace Conference

entry.title: Nonsmooth Nonconvex Optimization from Noisy Comparisons: Unbiased Gap Estimation and the Price of Preference Feedback
entry.summary: We study the minimization of $L$-Lipschitz, possibly nonsmooth and nonconvex $f:R^d\to R$ from noisy pairwise comparisons: comparing $x$ and $y$ returns a bit equal to $1$ with probability $σ((f(y)-f(x))/τ)$, for a known link $σ$ and temperature $τ$, and the goal is a $(δ,ε)$-Goldstein stationary point. We give an exactly unbiased estimator of the gap $f(y)-f(x)$ whenever $σ^{-1}$ is analytic on a lens in the complex plane, as for the logistic, probit and cauchit links: compare the pair until the outcome changes and return $\pmτ$ times a partial sum of the expansion coefficients of the inverse link, the harmonic number of the run length for the logistic link. It uses at most $1+1/(1-α)$ comparisons in expectation, $α$ the largest queried success probability, and has second moment of order the gap squared plus $τ^2$. With randomized smoothing and the online-to-nonconvex conversion this gives $O\big(d\,(1+d\,C_{link}/κ^2)\,L^2Δ_f/(δε^3)\big)$ comparisons when $Δ_f\ge Lδ$, where $κ$ is the ratio of the largest queried gap to $τ$, which the smoothing radius caps at a constant; relative to the optimal rate $O(dL^2Δ_f/(δε^3))$ for noisy value oracles, comparisons cost a factor $d/κ^2$. We prove that any comparison-based method needs $Ω(d^2τ^2/(ε^2δ^2))$ comparisons on a smooth convex subclass once $d\gtrsim(εδ/τ)^2$: in the comparison-noise-dominated regime the bounds agree in $d$ and $τ$, and a factor $Δ_f/(δε)$ remains open. Experiments illustrate the estimator's cost and variance and the $d^2$ growth of the gradient-estimator second moment.
entry.arxiv:comment: Updated title from: Nonsmooth Optimization with Zeroth Order Comparison Feedback

entry.title: A Network Simplex Framework For Discrete Unbalanced Optimal Transport
entry.summary: The network simplex method is a classical algorithm for minimum cost flow problems formulated as linear programs, that has attracted recent interest from the optimal transport community. Indeed, discrete optimal transport is a subclass of minimum cost flow for which network simplex techniques compute exact solutions while leveraging the inherent problem sparsity. However, extending these approaches to other, nonlinear optimal transport formulations has yet to be thoroughly investigated. In this paper, we adapt the network simplex algorithm to unbalanced optimal transport. Our proposed framework is applicable to various unbalanced formulations, and can be implemented explicitly in the most common cases, including semi-unbalanced optimal transport. The resulting algorithms are memory-efficient, and perform competitively with existing approaches, as shown by our experiments on a range of transport and barycenter calculations.

entry.title: The Integrality Gap of the Traveling Salesman Problem is $4/3$ if the LP Solution Has at Most $n+6$ Non-zero Components
entry.summary: We address the classical Dantzig - Fulkerson - Johnson formulation of the symmetric metric Traveling Salesman Problem and study the integrality gap of its linear relaxation, namely the Subtour Elimination Problem (SEP). This integrality gap is conjectured to be 4/3. We prove that, when solving a problem on n nodes, if the optimal SEP solution has at most n + 6 non-zero components, then the conjecture is true. To establish this result, we devise a new methodology that combines theoretical analysis and computational verification.

entry.title: A Variable Smoothing for Weakly Convex Composite Minimization with Manifold Constraint via Parametrization
entry.summary: In this paper, we address a manifold constrained nonsmooth optimization problem involving the composition of a weakly convex function and a smooth mapping under the availability of a parametrization of the manifold. To find a stationary point of the target problem, we propose a variable smoothing-type algorithm by combining the ideas of (i) translating the constrained problem into a Euclidean optimization problem with a parametrization of the constraint set; (ii) exploiting a sequence of smooth approximations of the objective constructed using the Moreau envelope. The proposed algorithm produces a vector sequence by the gradient descent update of a smooth approximation of the objective. In a case where the proximity operator of the weakly convex function is available, the proposed algorithm does not require any iterative solver for subproblems therein. By leveraging tools in the variational analysis, we show the so-called gradient consistency property, which is a key ingredient for smoothing-type algorithms, of the smooth approximations used in this paper. Based on the gradient consistency property, we establish a subsequential convergence guarantee of the proposed algorithm to a stationary point of the parameterized problem and clarify conditions, such as a submersion condition on the parametrization, under which the corresponding point is stationary for the original manifold constrained problem. Numerical experiments demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed algorithm.
entry.arxiv:comment: Published in Computational Optimization and Applications, 47 pages, 1 figure, 4 tables,

entry.title: Warm-IP: A Path-Following ADMM Warm Start for Interior-Point Quadratic Programming
entry.summary: Interior-point (IP) methods are powerful second-order optimization algorithms but can make slow progress during early iterations. We propose Warm-IP, a hybrid framework that combines a path-following variant of the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) with a primal--dual IP method. The ADMM phase generates a warm start that remains close to the central path, enabling the subsequent IP phase to rapidly refine the solution to high accuracy. We evaluate Warm-IP on a diverse collection of real-world and synthetic quadratic programming (QP) instances and compare it with leading commercial solvers (MOSEK and Gurobi) and open-source solvers (Clarabel, PIQP, and OSQP). We also curate and release a new benchmark of large-scale QPs from cancer radiotherapy treatment planning, built from real patient data and provided in canonical QP form, with instances containing hundreds of thousands of constraints. Warm-IP substantially outperforms existing solvers on large-scale problems. On the large-scale radiotherapy benchmark comprising 60 lung cancer cases, for example, Warm-IP solves an instance in 47 seconds on average with no failures, while the strongest competitors, MOSEK and Gurobi, average 55 seconds with failures on 23\% of the cases and roughly 240 seconds with no failures, respectively. To support reproducibility and future benchmarking, we publicly release the implementation and benchmark data through a \href{https://github.com/Radiotherapy-Optimization/Warm-IP}{GitHub repository}. These results demonstrate that appropriately warm-started IP methods can combine the rapid initial progress of first-order methods with the high-accuracy convergence of second-order methods.

entry.title: Adaptive Variance Reduction without Knowing Oracle Smoothness
entry.summary: Variance reduction improves the convergence rate of stochastic non-convex optimization under the average smoothness condition. Existing adaptive variance reduction methods are especially designed for average smoothness and do not adapt to standard smoothness. In this paper, we study how one algorithm can adapt to these two settings and the noiseless setting without knowing the smoothness constants or the variance bound. Given the gradient budget $T$, we develop a two-phase method. The first phase compares two independent gradients and switches to normalized momentum when their difference exceeds a threshold. This phase provides both a candidate with standard smooth and noiseless guarantees and also ensures a bounded expected function gap for the second variance reduction phase. The resulting rates are $O(T^{-1/3})$ under average smoothness, $O(T^{-1/4})$ under standard smoothness, and $O(T^{-1/2})$ without noise. When $T$ is unknown, we propose a method with two paths that attain the corresponding rates with logarithmic factors in the stochastic settings. Here, we use a variance reduction path to deal with average smoothness and employ the AdaGrad-Norm for standard smoothness and noiseless setting. Neither method restarts from the initial point or requires a growing number of oracle calls in each round.

entry.title: Randomized Momentum Transport with Cheap Predictors
entry.summary: Momentum methods such as STORM and second-order momentum track the gradient by adding a transport correction to momentum, at the cost of an extra oracle call per iteration. We introduce randomized momentum transport, which evaluates the correction with probability $q$ and otherwise uses a cheap prediction, with importance weighting that preserves the conditional mean and adds $(q^{-1}-1)$ times the prediction loss to the variance. Under transport-bias, second-moment, and residual-control assumptions, linear minimization oracle (LMO) updates, including normalized, sign, and exact spectral (Muon) directions, retain an $O(T^{-1/3})$ stationarity bound for each fixed $q>0$ with a single-gradient initialization. For unnormalized STORM, some $q<1$ lowers the leading coefficient of our sufficient gradient budget if and only if the gradient-difference noise modulus exceeds the smoothness constant, by at most about $10\%$. An online diagonal predictor admits a regret-to-convergence guarantee. At approximately equal oracle cost, querying a quarter of the corrections lowers the final training loss by $18$ to $43\%$ on MNIST1D and raises the test accuracy of Hessian-vector transport on CIFAR-10 by $1.5$ points.

entry.title: Optimal Algorithms for Nonsmooth Nonconvex Stochastic Optimization with Constraints
entry.summary: We present new algorithms for stochastic optimization problems in which the objective is neither smooth nor convex, subject to a convex constraint set. Our algorithms return a $(δ,\varepsilon)$-Goldstein stationary point, as recently defined for constrained problems by Liu et al. (2024), with improved complexities, and are the first to achieve optimal convergence rates for this task in several settings. In particular, we design projection-based and projection-free algorithms that achieve a $\widetilde O(δ^{-1}\varepsilon^{-3})$ rate using stochastic gradients, which we show to be optimal, and a $\widetilde O(dδ^{-1}\varepsilon^{-3})$ rate using zeroth-order queries, which is also optimal in its dependence on the dimension $d$ and improves over prior work. Notably, our lower bound is given in terms of the Frank-Wolfe gap and holds even for smooth problems, which is of independent interest. These results show that in nonconvex stochastic optimization, the convergence rate is degraded neither by the presence of constraints nor by nonsmoothness. Our analysis is based on a reduction to online linear optimization, extending a related technique from unconstrained optimization.

entry.title: Leak localisation with a measure source convection-diffusion model
entry.summary: Taking a variational approach, study the inverse problem of locating gas leaks from line-of-sight concentration measurements using a convection--diffusion model with the source term a Radon measure. By imposing sparsity-promoting regularisation on this measure, we recover point sources---identifying both their locations and intensities---rather than diffuse approximations. We jointly estimate the underlying physical convection (wind) and diffusion parameters. Our main theoretical contribution is the analysis of Lipschitz dependence of the forward solution of the convection--diffusion equation with respect to its parameters: the measure, and the convection and diffusion fields. Numerically, we employ a semi-grid-free optimisation approach for reconstructing the source measure. Our experiments demonstrate accurate localisation, highlighting the potential of the method for practical gas emission detection.

entry.title: Geometry-Aware Multi-Objective Optimization: Norm-Constrained Oracles with Entropic Weight Updates
entry.summary: Multiple-gradient descent is typically formulated in Euclidean geometry, whereas matrix-aware optimizers use directions induced by other norms. We analyze a single-loop multi-objective method combining a norm-constrained linear minimization oracle with entropic updates of task weights. For any finite-dimensional norm pair, we establish an $O(T^{-1/2})$ ergodic stationarity rate in the deterministic setting, deriving the required trajectory gradient bound from smoothness and lower-boundedness in the unregularized case. With stochastic gradients and a bounded-gradient assumption, one persistent blended-gradient momentum buffer yields an $O(T^{-1/4})$ rate whose leading term has no explicit dependence on the number of tasks. We also establish static regret for the inner weighting objective on arbitrary bounded gradient sequences and, with entropy regularization and a weight floor, iteration-wise inner-gap control after burn-in while retaining ergodic stationarity, conditional on a trajectory gradient bound. The optimal blended gradient can be nonunique in spectral and sign geometries, motivating a selection-independent inner gap. Our analysis extends the spectral construction studied by concurrent MOON to general norms. Experiments compare the method with existing multi-task optimizers and examine its oracle, weighting, and momentum choices.

entry.title: Estimation, Sensitivity Analysis, and Optimization of Distortion Risk Measures via Simulation
entry.summary: We present a simulation-based method for the estimation, sensitivity analysis, and optimization of distortion risk measures (DRMs), a class of performance measures that capture a wide range of risk attitudes through an underlying distortion function. Existing simulation approaches often approximate DRMs using numerical partitions or empirical distributions. We show that, when the distortion function is piecewise polynomial, the nonlinear structure of a DRM can be handled exactly, without introducing distortion discretization error, using only simulated system outputs. This representation enables the development of a computational method that integrates finite-difference techniques for sensitivity analysis and for solving a broad class of differentiable risk-based optimization problems. Under suitable conditions, we establish strong consistency and convergence rates for DRM estimation, sensitivity analysis, and optimization. We further extend the approach to non-polynomial distortion functions through polynomial approximation. Numerical experiments on synthetic and calibrated financial examples demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed approach across a range of applications.

entry.title: Stabilized SQP Method for Convex Piecewise Linear-Quadratic Composite Optimization Problems
entry.summary: This paper addresses the local convergence analysis of the stabilized sequential quadratic programming method for a class of composite optimization problems with convex piecewise linear- quadratic (CPLQ) modeling functions. We demonstrate that an appropriate second-order sufficient condition (SOSC) -formulated for composite problems- alone is sufficient to guarantee local superlin- ear convergence of the primal-dual sequence generated by this method. Furthermore, we examine the relaxation of the SOSC and show that it can be replaced with a weaker noncriticality of the associated Lagrange multiplier, provided, the modeling function is polyhedral and a relative interior condition is satisfied. We also present counterexamples showing that the relative interior condition is indispensable and that this relaxation fails for general CPLQ modeling functions.

entry.title: Relaxed Centralized Circumcentered-Reflection Methods for Convex Feasibility: Convergence and Finite Termination
entry.summary: Projection methods are among the most widely used techniques for solving convex feasibility problems due to their simplicity and robustness. However, classical projection-based algorithms and existing circumcentered-reflection methods generally provide only asymptotic convergence. In this paper, we introduce a relaxed version of the centralized circumcentered-reflection method (cCRM) obtained through an extrapolation of the circumcenter step. We first analyze the two-set case and then extend the proposed approach to the successive framework for multiple convex sets, including under- and over-relaxation and a backtracking strategy. The convergence analysis establishes Fejér monotonicity and global convergence under suitable conditions, while local error-bound assumptions yield linear convergence and standard regularity assumptions imply superlinear convergence. Motivated by finitely convergent projection methods based on perturbed feasible sets, we further investigate a perturbed relaxed formulation designed to achieve finite termination. Numerical experiments show good practical performance, comparable to and competitive with the finitely convergent PACA method. The results also provide clear numerical evidence of finite termination in the tested instances.

entry.title: Sum of Squares and Non Sum of Squares Regimes for the Toeplitz Bottcher Wenzel Form
entry.summary: Toeplitz matrices are among the simplest structured models of translation invariance, arising naturally in convolution, stationary covariance models, and discretizations of translation-invariant operators. For a pair of real matrices, the Böttcher--Wenzel form (BW form) is a nonnegative quartic measuring the gap in the corresponding commutator inequality. László conjectured that, when both matrices are Toeplitz, this quartic is a sum of squares for every matrix order. We show that the conjecture is false. More precisely, we identify an explicit family of corner-supported Toeplitz pairs, retaining only the outermost diagonals on the two sides, for which the associated BW form is not a sum of squares at all sufficiently large orders. The proof reduces the complete family of Gram representations to a finite complex test: its Gram-invariant part develops a strictly negative limiting direction, while the remaining Gram-dependent contribution vanishes. We also give an explicit sufficient threshold for the matrix order. The negative result is complemented by two positive regimes. If either Toeplitz factor is symmetric or skew-symmetric, then the corresponding BW form is SoS for every order, with the other factor allowed to be an arbitrary real Toeplitz matrix. For unrestricted Toeplitz pairs, we further prove SoS representability for every $2\le N\le50$, with formal Lean~4 verification through order 20. The large-order non-SoS theorem, including the explicit sufficient threshold, has also been formally verified in Lean 4.

entry.title: The Method of Ellipcenters for strongly convex minimization
entry.summary: This work is about ME, the Method of Ellipcenters. ME was recently introduced by these very authors as a first order accelerated scheme for unconstrained minimization. Its iterates are all centers of ellipses carefully designed to somehow capture ill-conditioning of the underlying optimization problem. In the first article on ME, we were able to prove that it converges with linear rate when the objective function is quadratic and strongly convex, while here we derive convergence for any differentiable strongly convex objective. This investigation was inspired by the great performance of ME in quadratic minimization against steepest descent with exact line search, FISTA, Barzilai-Borwein and Conjugate Gradient. The experiments we carry out now, make ME even more attractive from the numerical point of view. On top of that, the theory seems promising for quite more general settings.

entry.title: Private and Distributionally Robust Federated Multiclass Classification
entry.summary: Fault diagnosis in asset-intensive industries requires multiclass models trained on noisy, sensitive data collected across geographically distributed client sites. Federated learning enables collaborative training without centralizing data, but most approaches do not provide formal privacy guarantees for individual records stored at client sites and can degrade under label noise. To address these limitations, we develop a differentially private, distributionally robust framework for federated multiclass classification that provides sample-level privacy for records stored at each client. We build on a federated Wasserstein distributionally robust multiclass objective with the Crammer-Singer loss, solved using an Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM)-based algorithm. To protect the released client updates, our method injects calibrated Gaussian noise into the proximal linearized client updates of both the local model and the local distributionally robust variable before aggregation at the central server, and we quantify the cumulative privacy loss using the moments accountant. We provide per-round sample-level $(ε,δ)$-differential privacy guarantees and an overall composed privacy guarantee across all training rounds, together with convergence results and an explicit privacy-utility tradeoff. Experiments on simulated industrial fault data and UCI benchmark datasets show that our method outperforms differentially private federated empirical risk minimization and stochastic gradient descent baselines in most tested settings, with the largest gains under strong privacy-induced noise.

entry.title: An inverse spectral problem for the wave equation with a varying Robin parameter at the boundary
entry.summary: An inverse spectral problem for a $(1+1)$-dimensional wave equation with wave speed $c(x)$ is considered. The spectral data consist of the eigenvalues of the Neumann--Dirichlet problem for the operator $-c^2(x)\partial_x^2$ together with their derivatives with respect to a Robin parameter at the boundary. We propose a two-step recovery procedure. In the first step, the Neumann-to-Dirichlet map $Λ$ is reconstructed from the spectral data using the results of arXiv/0406582. In the second step, the reconstructed $Λ$ is used within the regularization strategy for the boundary control method presented in arXiv:1509.04478. As an improvement, the regularization of the control problems employs a weighted combination of $L^2$ and $H^1$ penalty terms, and we prove a uniform convergence result for the family of optimal controls, thereby allowing the regularization parameters to be tuned simultaneously. We also prove that the forward spectral map, which assigns to a wave speed its spectral data, is Lipschitz continuous, and that the inverse spectral map underlying the reconstruction procedure is Hölder continuous on a subclass of wave speeds. The method is implemented numerically and validated on both smooth and piecewise smooth wave speed profiles. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the recovery of the wave speed exhibits high accuracy and robustness.
entry.arxiv:comment: 51 pages, 8 figures, 2 tables. Code available at https://github.com/pkulikov239/bcm-inverse-spectral

entry.title: Lower Bounds for Randomized Linear-Oracle Optimization over Strongly Convex Sets
entry.summary: Recent results [arXiv:2602.04378, arXiv:2602.22608] have established worst-case objective-error lower bounds of order $1/T^2$ after $T$ linear minimization oracle (LMO) calls, matching the upper bound [arXiv:1406.1305] in its dependence on $T$ and thereby resolving a long-standing open question. Upon close inspection, however, both lower bounds are somewhat brittle. The first [arXiv:2602.04378] applies only to the standard Frank--Wolfe algorithm, and, as we show, its prescribed slow exact-line-search trajectories can amplify sufficiently small initialization errors exponentially, corresponding to roughly one additional bit of initialization accuracy per iteration. The second [arXiv:2602.22608] obtains lower bounds for any deterministic LMO-based first-order method via a resisting oracle that adversarially adapts to the queries of the algorithm. In both cases it is conceivable that randomization may circumvent these lower bounds; in particular, neither establishes a lower bound for unrestricted randomized first-order LMO methods. We close this gap by proving an $Ω(L\operatorname{diam}(S)^2/T^2)$ distributional lower bound for randomized first-order linear minimization oracle methods over strongly convex sets. While our construction reuses the family of [arXiv:2602.22608], our proof characterizes the conditional distribution of the hidden permutation after adaptive queries and bounds the expected decrease of a combinatorial statistic controlling optimizer variance. We further show that the same error threshold holds with probability at least $3/4$ and yields a stopping-time tail bound.

entry.title: A Unifying Framework for Global Optimization: From Theory to Formalization
entry.summary: We introduce an abstract measure___theoretic framework that serves as a tool to rigorously study stochastic iterative global optimization algorithms as a unified class. The framework is formulated in terms of probability kernels, which, via the Ionescu--Tulcea theorem, induce probability measures on the space of sequences of algorithm iterations, endowed with two intuitive properties. This framework answers the need for a general, implementation___independent formalism in the analysis of such algorithms, providing a starting point for formalizing global optimization results in proof-assistants. To illustrate the relevance of our tool, we show that common algorithms fit naturally in the framework, and we also use it to give a rigorous proof of a general consistency theorem for stochastic iterative global optimization algorithms (Proposition 3 of (Malherbe, et al., 2017). This proof and the entire framework are formalized in the Lean proof assistant. This formalization both ensures the correctness of the definitions and proofs, and provides a basis for future machine-assisted formalizations in the field.

entry.title: Boundary stabilization of multi-dimensional first-order quasilinear hyperbolic systems
entry.summary: We study the long-time behaviour of multi-dimensional first-order symmetrizable quasilinear hyperbolic systems with nonlinear feedback boundary conditions. Assuming strict interior and boundary Lyapunov inequalities for the linearized system and non-characteristic boundaries, we prove global existence for small initial data and exponential H^s decay, with s>d/2+1 an integer. We consider both bounded smooth domains and flat periodic cylinders, and illustrate the results with physical examples and numerical simulations.

entry.title: Infinitesimal Operator World Models: Finite-Sample Guarantees for Offline Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary: Continuous-time stochastic processes underlie many natural and engineered systems. In healthcare, autonomous driving, and industrial control, direct interaction with the environment is often unsafe or impractical, motivating offline reinforcement learning from historical data. However, there is limited statistical understanding of the approximation errors inherent in learning policies from offline datasets. We address this by linking reinforcement learning to the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation and proposing an operator-theoretic algorithm based on a simple dynamic programming recursion. Specifically, we represent our world model in terms of the infinitesimal generator of controlled diffusion processes learned in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space. By integrating statistical learning methods and operator theory, we establish global convergence of the value function under sufficiently small generator-approximation error and derive explicit finite-sample guarantees with bounds tied directly to system properties such as smoothness and stability. Our theoretical and proof-of-concept results indicate that operator-based approaches may hold promise for solving offline reinforcement learning using continuous-time optimal control.
entry.arxiv:journal_ref: IEEE Open Journal of Control Systems, 01 October 2026

entry.title: Stationary Ergodic Mean-field Games of Constrained Singular Controls
entry.summary: We study a stationary ergodic mean-field game of scalar type where the representative player controls a diffusion through two-sided singular controls exerted only at the jump times of an independent Poisson process. For each mean-field parameter, we solve the novel constrained ergodic singular control problem, proving that the optimal policy is of threshold type: the diffusion is reset at Poisson arrival times to the nearest boundary point of an interval. Our explicit probabilistic derivation of the stationary distributions induced by Poissonian threshold singular controls is a key contribution of independent interest. This distribution is used to construct the mean-field fixed-point map. We prove existence and uniqueness of the stationary mean-field equilibrium by combining the stationary density with the monotonicity and continuity of the optimal thresholds in the mean-field parameter. The model provides a tractable framework for a case study of partially reversible investment with singular adjustments under exogenous intervention constraints.

entry.title: Learning to accelerate Krasnosel'skii-Mann fixed-point iterations with guarantees
entry.summary: We introduce a principled learning to optimize (L2O) framework for solving fixed-point problems involving general nonexpansive mappings. Our idea is to deliberately inject summable perturbations into a standard Krasnosel'skii-Mann iteration to improve its average-case performance over a specific distribution of problems while retaining its convergence guarantees. Under a metric sub-regularity assumption, we prove that the proposed parametrization includes only iterations that locally achieve linear convergence-up to a vanishing bias term-and that it encompasses all iterations that do so at a sufficiently fast rate. We then demonstrate how our framework can be used to augment several widely-used operator splitting methods to accelerate the solution of structured monotone inclusion problems, and validate our approach on a best approximation problem using an L2O-augmented Douglas-Rachford splitting algorithm.

entry.title: A Scalable Learned Iterative Solver for Nonlinear MPC via Temporal Decomposition
entry.summary: Nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) can be applied to large nonlinear systems with complex objectives while enforcing constraints, but the cost of solving the underlying optimization problems limits real-time application for systems with fast dynamics or many states. Neural networks can reduce this online cost by approximating the control law, but may violate constraints and typically require many precomputed optimizer solutions for training. The learning-based iterative solver for constrained optimization (LISCO) instead learns to predict primal-dual steps toward satisfaction of the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions through self-supervised training without precomputed solutions, but its dense, monolithic architecture grows with the prediction horizon. We remove this horizon dependence by exploiting the temporal structure of the problem in the solver architecture, which makes the network size independent of the horizon while leaving the training loss and the solver iteration unchanged. A closed-loop resampling strategy further aligns the training distribution with closed-loop operation at no additional sampling cost. On an economic NMPC benchmark of a CSTR cascade, the proposed solver scales to larger problems than monolithic LISCO and achieves median speedups of up to a factor of four over IPOPT. In closed loop, it achieves comparable control performance to IPOPT with no observed constraint violations.

entry.title: Beyond QAOA: A Review of AI and Quantum Computing for Adaptive Combinatorial Optimization
entry.summary: Near-term quantum approaches to combinatorial optimization are limited by qubit counts, circuit fidelity, sampling cost, and the difficulty of encoding constraints, while machine learning is increasingly used to configure and control quantum optimization workflows. We call such workflows adaptive: decisions conventionally fixed in advance, from formulation and penalties to shot budgets, backends, and whether to invoke a quantum processor at all, are made by learned policies that respond to the instance, the progress of the solve, or the hardware. This review examines three paradigms, AI for quantum optimization, quantum for AI-driven optimization, and AI-quantum co-optimization, and organizes the literature by the decision being learned rather than by application. A structured search identified a 119-paper corpus, of which 67 papers form an evidence core coded in detail. The evidence is considerably stronger for AI-assisted quantum optimization than for the reverse direction: learning already reduces quantum evaluations, improves initialization, supports decomposition and penalty control, and mitigates noise, whereas evidence that quantum computation improves learned optimizers remains largely confined to small-scale simulation. Experimental controls are thin: of 52 studies in the three paradigms, 22 include no classical baseline, the quantum contribution is fully isolated in 10 of 24 where an ablation applies, and the median largest experiment uses 16 qubits. We introduce an M0-M5 evidence hierarchy, from simulation to practical quantum advantage, and find no broadly convincing result at the highest level. We argue that scaling is increasingly a systems problem: the question is not only whether a problem fits on a quantum processor, but how classical and quantum resources should be allocated across the optimization process.
entry.arxiv:comment: 36 pages, 5 figures, 7 tables; supplementary evidence matrix included as ancillary file. v2: clarified terminologies, co-optimization definition and evidence denominators; added references, minor corrections

entry.title: Utility-Based Recovery Risk Measures: Redundancy and Approximation for Portfolio Optimization
entry.summary: Recovery risk measures incorporate explicit liability-recovery requirements into asset-liability risk assessment. We study their specialization to optimized certainty equivalents (OCEs), allowing the underlying utility specification to vary across recovery levels and encompassing Recovery Average Value at Risk (RecAV@R) as a special case. For finite recovery specifications, we use the dual penalty representation to characterize redundant recovery regimes and derive position-independent screening conditions. For a subfamily of the Cressie-Read power-divergence family, including entropic and truncated-quadratic specifications, we obtain an exact characterization on atomless probability spaces: universal redundancy is equivalent to a two-dimensional convex-hull condition involving recovery levels and divergence-scale parameters. On such spaces, universal redundancy for RecAV@R reduces to pairwise dominance, whereas for power-divergence OCEs it can arise from the joint effect of several recovery regimes. For nonlinear OCE utilities, we develop a certified piecewise-linear approximation framework for portfolio optimization. In finite-scenario models, the approximating problems are finite-dimensional linear programs, while utility approximation errors transfer directly to the Recovery OCE, yielding explicit error bounds and convergence rates. Uniform approximation over the portfolio domain further implies convergence of optimal values and stability of optimal solutions. A numerical asset-liability study illustrates the effects of recovery-dependent risk preferences and the accuracy and convergence of the approximation.

entry.title: An Optimal Control Approach to Finite-Time Stabilization of Linear Systems
entry.summary: This paper presents a finite-time stabilization method for the integrator chain via optimal control techniques by introducing a tailored cost function. We analyze key properties of the resulting value function to derive the corresponding Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation. Numerical simulations illustrate the effectiveness of the approach.
entry.arxiv:journal_ref: 23rd IFAC World Congress, International Federation of Automatic Control, Aug 2026, Pusan, South Korea

entry.title: Minimum-Energy Control for Stochastic Linear Systems
entry.summary: The open-loop minimum-energy control (MEC) problem asks for control inputs that minimize the control energy while ensuring the terminal state reaches a desired value. In this paper, we study the open-loop MEC problem for stochastic linear time-invariant systems. We consider a variety of stochastic constraints that enforce the terminal error to be \emph{small}, and show that Stochastic MEC (SMEC) problem can be formulated as a QCQP. We obtain the optimal solution for SMEC and show that it generalizes the well-known Deterministic MEC problem by introducing novel stochastic variants of controllability and Gramian matrices. Finally, we show that there exists a fundamental lower bound on the optimal control energy which cannot be overcome by increasing the time horizon of the problem.

entry.title: The Riemannian Convex Bundle Method
entry.summary: We introduce the convex bundle method to solve convex, non-smooth optimization problems on Riemannian manifolds of bounded sectional curvature. Each step of our method is based on a model that involves the convex hull of previously collected subgradients, parallelly transported into the current serious iterate. This approach generalizes the dual form of classical bundle subproblems in Euclidean space. We prove that, under mild conditions, the convex bundle method converges to a minimizer. Several numerical examples implemented using Manopt$.$jl illustrate the performance of the proposed method and compare it to the subgradient method, the cyclic proximal point algorithm, as well as the proximal bundle method.

entry.title: Circuit-Embedded Feeder-State Reconstruction for Low-Voltage Distribution Networks under Extreme Measurement Sparsity
entry.summary: Low-voltage (LV) distribution feeders increasingly require internal state information, yet real-time telemetry is often limited to feeder-head active and reactive power, while downstream demand and production are described only by static contract metadata. This paper proposes a physics-based AC circuit-embedding reconstruction framework for this extreme-sparsity regime. Feeder-head measurements, matched metadata, and class-level profiles first determine bus-level load and production priors. These priors parameterize auxiliary constant-power elements coupled to the physical feeder through impedance branches, and the feeder state is reconstructed by solving the resulting nonlinear AC circuit equilibrium. The resulting AC equilibrium enforces the assigned virtual-element powers, while weighted least squares (WLS) reconciles measurements and pseudo-measurements through weighted residual fitting. The method is evaluated on a real 459-bus Portuguese LV feeder model using an in-sample-calibrated synthetic benchmark of 672 fifteen-minute snapshots. The proposed method converged for all 672 snapshots and achieved voltage RMSE, MAE, and maximum absolute error of 0.0033, 0.0014, and 0.0337 p.u., respectively, outperforming both static-prior WLS baselines. Under the same constructed priors, matched-prior WLS achieved a lower RMSE of 0.0029 p.u., while the proposed circuit embedding reconstructs the feeder state by solving the nonlinear AC equilibrium, bypassing WLS residual fitting entirely and requiring no specification or tuning of pseudo-measurement variances.

entry.title: Optimal Control of Prox-Regular Sweeping Processes with Variable Time
entry.summary: The paper is devoted to a broad class of optimal control problems governed by constrained sweeping processes with controlled dynamics, controlled prox-regular moving sets, and variable time included in the optimization process. Employing an advanced version of the method of discrete approximations, we verify its well-posedness with appropriate strong convergence of feasible and optimal solutions. This approach leads us to considering a parametric family of discrete-time controlled sweeping processes, which are reduced in turn to nondynamic mathematical programs with special types of geometric and functional constraints. Invoking powerful tools of first-order and second-order variational analysis and generalized differentiation, we derive necessary optimality conditions for discrete-time and then---by passing to the limit over the diminishing step of discretization---continuous-time controlled sweeping processes. A crucial role in our device is played by explicit coderivative evaluations of set-valued mapping associated with the sweeping dynamics. In this way, we establish novel necessary optimality conditions for local minimizers of continuous-time controlled sweeping processes that contain absolutely continuous and BV adjoint arcs, local and global maximization conditions, $L^2$ active set multipliers, vector measures generated by sweeping and control constraints, and free-time transversality condition expressed through the averaged Hamiltonian. For suitably selected multipliers, we also obtain nondegenerate forms of these conditions when the optimal trajectory starts on the boundary of the moving set. The efficiency of the obtained results is illustrated by some examples related to practical modeling.

entry.title: Bayesian dynamic scheduling of multipurpose batch processes under incomplete look-ahead information
entry.summary: Multipurpose batch processes become increasingly popular in manufacturing industries since they adapt to low-volume, high-value products and shifting demands. These processes often operate in a dynamic environment, which faces disturbances such as processing delays and demand changes. To minimise long-term cost and system nervousness (i.e., disruptive changes to schedules), schedulers must design rescheduling strategies to address such disturbances effectively. Existing methods often assume complete look-ahead information over the scheduling horizon. This assumption contrasts with realistic situations where schedulers can only access incomplete look-ahead information. Sticking with existing methods may lead to suboptimal long-term costs and high-level system nervousness. In this work we propose a Bayesian dynamic scheduling method. Our method relies on learning a Bayesian Network from the probability distribution of disturbances. Specifically, the Bayesian Network represents how likely each operation will be impacted by disturbances. During the online execution, when new disturbances become observed, this method updates the posterior distribution and therefore guides the rescheduling strategy. We compare our method with the existing periodic rescheduling strategy (which generates new schedules from scratch at fixed intervals) on four benchmark problems. Computational results show that our method achieves statistically better long-term costs and system nervousness. In the theoretical aspect, we prove that if disturbances are mutually independent, the impact-quantifying variables inherently satisfy the independence assumptions required by Bayesian Networks. As an implication, practitioners can extend the method to other scheduling problems (such as job shop scheduling and continuous processes), given that they define the problem-specific dependencies between operations.

entry.title: Data-Driven Stochastic Optimal Control in Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Spaces
entry.summary: This paper proposes a fully data-driven approach for optimal control of nonlinear control-affine systems represented by a stochastic diffusion. The focus is on the scenario where both the nonlinear dynamics and stage cost functions are unknown, while only a control penalty function and constraints are provided. To this end, we embed state probability densities into a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) to leverage recent advances in operator regression, thereby identifying Markov transition operators associated with controlled diffusion processes. This operator learning approach integrates naturally with convex operator-theoretic Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman recursions that scale linearly with state dimensionality, effectively solving a wide range of nonlinear optimal control problems. Numerical results demonstrate its ability to address diverse nonlinear control tasks, including the depth regulation of an autonomous underwater vehicle.
entry.arxiv:journal_ref: Engineering Applications of Artificial Intelligence, 1 October 2026, Volume 181, Part 6, Article 115698

entry.title: Riemannian Shape Analysis of the Corpus Callosum in Kendall Space: Aging and Alzheimer's Disease
entry.summary: The corpus callosum (CC) is a major white-matter structure and a well-established marker of brain aging, but most studies quantify it using scalar summaries that discard its boundary geometry. We present a Riemannian shape-space framework \cite{fletcher2013geodesic-regression} for analyzing age-related morphological change in the midsagittal CC, applied to the OASIS-1 cohort. Each contour is represented by $128$ landmarks and embedded into Kendall shape space, where translation, rotation, and scale are removed. We derive a multivariate geodesic regression with exact Riemannian gradients and use the fitted age-velocity field to localize age-related deformation to five anatomical sub-regions. In the cognitively normal cohort ($n = 252$), geodesic regression outperforms the Euclidean linear benchmark ($R^2 = 0.1355$ vs.\ $0.1216$). Regional energy is anterior-dominant: the Genu carries $46.1\%$ and the Anterior Body $23.3\%$ of total age-related shape change, together accounting for $\sim 69\%$ despite comprising only $\sim 41\%$ of landmarks. Signed projections confirm the ordering (Genu $r = 0.562$; Anterior Body $r = 0.507$). In contrast, age explains less than $0.5\%$ of shape variance in Alzheimer's disease ($n = 88$), indicating that the disease disrupts the healthy aging trajectory. A tangent-space classifier achieves an age-group AUC of $0.791$ from the 2D contour alone, exceeding a recent volumetric benchmark ($0.67$).

entry.title: Featurized Occupation Measures for Structured Global Search in Numerical Optimal Control
entry.summary: Numerical optimal control is split between globally structured but dimensionally intractable Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman (HJB) methods and scalable but local trajectory optimization. We introduce Featurized Occupation Measures (FOM), a finite-dimensional primal--dual interface where HJB subsolutions guide primal search and primal occupation data can inform certificate refinement. Explicit and implicit realizations, based on finite Liouville tests and rollout-sampled residuals, are proved asymptotically consistent with the exact occupation-measure LP. FOM also identifies when HJB-type certificates avoid full state-space representation. For factor graphs induced by compatible passivity-based interconnections, blockwise HJB inequalities yield block-additive OM-dual certificates, including blockwise approximate variants. The curse of dimensionality is then shifted from state dimension to interconnection topology. Approximate certificates remain reusable under time shifts and bounded model perturbations, with explicit degradation bounds. A static obstacle-avoidance benchmark illustrates how tighter certificates improve sample-based global search.

entry.title: Classical and Quantum Heuristics for the Binary Paint Shop Problem
entry.summary: The Binary Paint Shop Problem (BPSP) is an $\mathsf{APX}$-hard optimisation problem arising in automotive manufacturing: given a sequence of $2n$ cars, comprising $n$ distinct models each appearing twice, the task is to decide which of two colours to paint each car so that the two occurrences of each model are painted differently, while minimising consecutive colour swaps. Performance is measured by the paint swap ratio -- the average number of colour changes per car -- which directly affects production efficiency and cost. Prior work showed that the Quantum Approximate Optimisation Algorithm (QAOA) at depth $p=7$ achieves a ratio of $0.393$, outperforming the then-best-known classical heuristic, Recursive Greedy, with a proven asymptotic expected ratio of $0.4$ [Phys. Rev. A 104, 012403 (2021)]. More recently, the Recursive Star Greedy (RSG) heuristic was proposed with a conjectured expected ratio of $0.361$. Here, we formally reduce BPSP to weighted MaxCut, yielding an exact Ising formulation, and benchmark two state-of-the-art low-depth QAOA variants -- eXpressive QAOA and Recursive QAOA -- at $p=1$ (denoted XQAOA$_1$ and RQAOA$_1$) against four classical BPSP heuristics. Across instances ranging from $2^7$ to $2^{12}$ cars, XQAOA$_1$ achieves an average paint-swap ratio of $0.357$; in our instance-wise benchmarks, it outperforms RQAOA$_1$ on almost all instances and each of the four classical baselines, including RSG, on every instance. Surprisingly, RQAOA$_1$ deteriorates with problem size despite employing provably near-optimal QAOA$_1$ parameters at each recursive step, eventually falling behind RSG at the largest sizes. To our knowledge, this is the first report of size-dependent performance degradation of RQAOA$_1$ at scale. In contrast, XQAOA$_1$ remains stable across all tested sizes, with no evidence of size-dependent degradation.
entry.arxiv:comment: 32 pages, 3 figures. Final revised version accepted for publication in Physical Review Applied

entry.title: Structure-Aware Online Optimization of the Age of Information with Unknown System Statistics
entry.summary: Timely information dissemination is essential in modern communication systems, where low informational latency is critical for networked control, monitoring, and real-time decision-making. The Age of Information (AoI) has emerged as a fundamental metric for quantifying information freshness at the receiver. A key challenge in AoI optimization is selecting the update generation rate: infrequent updates lead to stale information, whereas overly frequent updates increase queueing delays. We develop a structure-aware, data-driven framework for adaptive AoI optimization modeled as single-server queues with unknown system statistics. Our key idea is to exploit analytical representations of the AoI gradient, which depend on a finite-dimensional collection of system quantities that can be estimated from observations collected during system operation. This reduces the online learning problem to estimating the quantities required by the gradient, rather than learning the AoI objective as a black box. We propose an online stochastic approximation algorithm that jointly estimates these quantities and optimizes the update generation rate. We prove almost sure convergence of the algorithm to the optimal update generation rate under mild regularity and moment conditions, despite the temporal dependence induced by the underlying queueing process. We demonstrate the framework in four representative incomplete-information settings, including FCFS queues with unknown service characteristics or hidden background traffic, a preemptive LCFS system with partial observations, and a generate-at-will system with threshold waiting.

entry.title: Representing the Non-dominated Set of Multi-objective Optimization Problems with Polyhedral Ordering Cones
entry.summary: In the literature, research on representing the non-dominated set has focused almost exclusively on multi-objective optimization problems with Pareto-dominance. However, general ordering cones are used to incorporate preferences of decision makers into the optimization process and to model other specific types of optimization problems, such as ordinal optimization problems. In this work, we consider several representation approaches based on representation relations in the context of multi-objective optimization problems with polyhedral ordering cones. Our main research question is whether existing theory and solution approaches developed for the Pareto case can be used to address the more general setting.

entry.title: Model-free Reinforcement Learning for Continuous Time and State: A Stochastic Maximum Principle Approach
entry.summary: This paper develops a model-free reinforcement learning (RL) algorithm based on the stochastic maximum principle for continuous-time stochastic control problems with continuous state and action spaces. For a parameterized Markovian policy, we establish the existence of the decoupling field for the adjoint backward stochastic differential equation, which allows the Hamiltonian gradient to be represented as a deterministic function of time and state. We then learn this Hamiltonian gradient directly from data and incorporate it into a policy gradient scheme with inexact gradients. We establish the convergence of the resulting policy gradient algorithm and establish the corresponding error estimates. Under suitable conditions on learning rates, exploration parameters, and approximation errors, the objective values converge and the $L^2$-norm of the policy gradient vanishes asymptotically. We further show that the proposed SMP-based policy gradient representation is equivalent to the existing continuous-time deterministic policy gradient representation based on the advantage-rate function. The effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed RL algorithm are demonstrated by numerical experiments.

entry.title: Tight Guarantees for Static Policies in Vehicle Sharing Networks
entry.summary: We study pricing in a vehicle sharing network with $N$ locations and $C$ vehicles, motivated by on-demand bike, scooter, and car sharing, as well as robotaxi and ride sharing services. Customers request directed trips between locations, with travel times following general distributions, and leave without service if no vehicle is available. Pricing affects both demand for trips and the distribution of vehicles across locations. Computing an optimal dynamic pricing policy is challenging because the system state depends on the number of vehicles available at each location and in transit (including how long they have been traveling), motivating the use of simple static policies that offer a fixed price for each trip. For any number of vehicles and locations, we establish a tight performance guarantee for static pricing relative to optimal dynamic pricing. The guarantee holds for any concave objective functions (including revenue rate) and general travel time distributions. Our tight guarantee is bounded below by $ \frac{C}{C + \min \{ C -1, \sqrt{ CN} \} }$ (over 50%), achieving the first universal, non-asymptotic constant factor guarantee. We also prove that the optimal static policy can be efficiently computed by solving a convex optimization problem. Finally, we extend our performance guarantee to the setting with supply redirection.

entry.title: A Palais-Smale type condition for optimal control problems
entry.summary: We consider an optimal control problem with a general control constraint and a fixed initial state, for which convexity assumptions are absent. To establish the existence of optimal pairs, we introduce a control version of the Palais-Smale type condition adapted from critical point theory and prove that optimal pairs exist under this condition (see Theorem 2.1). Subsequently, we verify that a specific class of optimal control problems satisfies our Palais-Smale type condition (see Proposition 2.1). Furthermore, as an application, we present an example (Example 3.1) and show that, to the best of our knowledge, no existing result can be applied to establish the existence of an optimal pair in this case (see Section 3.1.1). Example 3.2 shows that finitely many Pontryagin maximum principle candidates do not guarantee the existence of an optimal control. Finally, Example 3.3 demonstrates that the proposed Palais-Smale type condition is sufficient, but not necessary, for the existence of optimal controls.

entry.title: Leveraging Christoffel-Darboux Kernels to Strengthen Moment-SOS Relaxations
entry.summary: The classical Moment-SOS hierarchy allows one to approximate the global minimum of a polynomial optimization problem through semidefinite relaxations of increasing accuracy. For many optimization problems, however, moving to higher relaxation orders quickly becomes computationally prohibitive. While this difficulty is commonly addressed by exploiting structural properties such as symmetry or sparsity, we explore a complementary direction: strengthening a low-order relaxation using information contained in its own pseudo-moment solution. To this end, we leverage Christoffel-Darboux kernels to identify regions that are compatible with the current pseudo-moment information and use them to construct additional polynomial constraints. We propose two mechanisms: the first, denoted $\HH$, is based on successive global Christoffel restrictions, while the second, denoted $\hh$, combines marginal Christoffel information with an available local solution. For $\HH$, we establish a uniform separation property for successive pseudo-moment solutions and geometric convergence of the fixed-order bounds on a particular subclass of knapsack problems. Moreover, for specific Boolean quadratic problems, we derive an explicit $\hh$ selection rule and establish conditions under which the resulting marginal constraints preserve all global minimizers. Numerical experiments on dense and sparse nonconvex quadratically constrained quadratic programs show that the resulting strengthened low-order relaxations can significantly improve the initial bounds, sometimes attaining exactness, while remaining substantially cheaper than solving higher-order relaxations.

entry.title: Dynamic Matching with Abandonment: Optimal Guarantees via Static Priority Policies
entry.summary: We study stochastic dynamic matching with abandonment, a fundamental model in which agents of different types arrive over time, may abandon the market while waiting, and can be matched in pairs for rewards that depend on their types. No online policy can guarantee more than $0.5$ of the omniscient benchmark, which knows all arrival and departure times. Whether this guarantee is achievable has been a central open problem, even in special cases. We resolve this problem by showing that, on every instance, a simple static priority policy, which is computable in polynomial time, earns at least $0.5$ of the omniscient benchmark. This establishes that the optimal competitive ratio is exactly $0.5$, improving the previous best guarantee of 0.192 for the general model [Li et al. 2026; Collina et al. 2020] Our analysis rests on a key stochastic result, which is a new lower bound on the probability that some agent from a given set of types is available. Building on this bound, we develop two approaches: a primal approach that reads the priorities from an optimal solution of a novel linear program, and a dual approach that assigns a ``value'' to each type, and prioritizes matches with high ``surplus'' (reward minus value of involved agents). These values are the unique solution of a fixed-point equation derived from linear programming duality. We also show that the two approaches are closely connected.

entry.title: Deflating the Hessian: Rank-4 W4A4 Quantization for Multimodal Diffusion Transformers
entry.summary: In diffusion transformers, low-rank branches can mitigate 4-bit weight--activation (W4A4) post-training quantization (PTQ) loss by decomposing each weight into a low-bit residual and a high-precision low-rank component. Existing low-rank PTQ approaches, however, either optimize low-rank compensation and residual quantization separately, often requiring higher ranks, or rely on second-order weight updates without explicitly modeling activation quantization error, which becomes particularly pronounced under 4-bit quantization. To address these limitations, we present HSVDQuant, a unified framework modeling low-rank-assisted W4A4 PTQ as a coupled calibration problem and deriving optimization-based solvers from the joint objective. Eliminating the output-side low-rank factor yields a deflated Hessian that discounts residual errors already captured by the low-rank component, while an activation-noise surrogate is incorporated to suppress activation quantization error. Across five diffusion backbones, rank-4 HSVDQuant consistently outperforms rank-4 SVDQuant in PSNR and LPIPS. It further surpasses rank-32 SVDQuant on SANA-1.6B, FLUX.1-schnell, and FLUX.1-dev with an $8\times$ smaller rank and up to $6.25\times$ faster quantization. Furthermore, on the Qwen3-8B LLM, rank-4 HSVDQuant improves MMLU accuracy from 61.50% to 68.17% over rank-32 SVDQuant. Overall, HSVDQuant achieves better W4A4 performance with substantially lower rank and quantization cost.

entry.title: Sequential Conformal Calibration under Recursive Selection
entry.summary: Conformal prediction provides finite-sample, distribution-free coverage guarantees that can support decision-making in specific settings. In multistage problems, earlier decisions determine the populations relevant to later calibration. When later scores are refit using earlier calibration results, reusing those cases for ranking need not preserve exchangeability with a surviving test case. We study sequential conformal calibration with a fresh fold at each stage: conditional on earlier folds, the selected fold scores and the surviving test score are exchangeable. This yields finite-sample coverage guarantees for every prefix of the decision sequence. For atomless survivor score distributions, we derive a universal Binomial-thinned Beta chain for the realized coverage process. Its law depends only on fold sizes and target levels, even under predictable refitting, and yields exact coverage slack, abstention probabilities, and calibration-conditional guarantees. We further characterize the tradeoff between freshness and data reuse. For fixed scores, strict-survivor reuse is exactly valid. For adaptive scores refit using past calibration data, reusing survivors can incur worst-case rank loss, while blocked designs provide an intermediate option between full reuse and stagewise fresh folds. As a case study, we apply the framework to serial multi-echelon inventory problem and propose a sequential conditional-quantile formulation. Each stock level is learned as a context-dependent quantile of cumulative demand among scenarios satisfying earlier no-backlog constraints. We connect these targets to common-shift stationarity and derive decision-level implications for the resulting calibrated policies. In a three-echelon simulation, fresh-fold refitting achieves 81.98% final-prefix coverage against an 81.82% target while reducing mean cost by 5.5% relative to the Bonferroni baseline.

entry.title: A volume-controlled level-set method for topology optimization
entry.summary: Topology optimization typically involves a geometric volume/mass constraint due to the limited use of material. As a popular technique for topology optimization, the level-set method typically employs the Lagrange method, the penalty method, or the augmented Lagrangian approach to address the volume constraint. This requires careful parameter tuning and may lead to non-monotonic changes in the objective. In this paper, we present a new volume-controlled level-set method for topology optimization. By imposing a scalar weighted volume?compatibility constraint in a modified Stokes-type extension-regularization problem, the velocity is made volume compatible at the beginning of each frozen transport interval. At the continuous level, we prove that the initial rate of change of the regularized volume vanishes and that the subsequent frozen-velocity drift is of order $T^2$; under a narrow-band assumption, the corresponding constant is independent of the smoothing parameter. For the discontinuous Galerkin spatial semi-discretization of the level-set transport equation, we derive a quantitative regularized-volume drift estimate that displays the dependence on the smoothing parameter, spatial mesh size, transport time, and discrete velocity. The effectiveness of the present algorithm is demonstrated through the minimum compliance problem for linear elasticity, the eigenfrequency maximization for structural vibration, and the minimum energy dissipation problem for Stokes flows.

entry.title: AI-Mediation in Retail Markets: Revenue Effects and Assortment Optimization
entry.summary: AI shopping assistants increasingly influence which products consumers consider. We study retail assortment planning under AI mediation, where a retailer chooses a catalog, an AI intermediary forms a customer-facing shortlist, and the customer chooses from that shortlist according to a multinomial logit model. We consider both deterministic mediation, in which the AI follows a fixed segment-specific ranking, and stochastic mediation based on the Plackett-Luce model. Empirically, we construct a dataset of product rankings from leading AI models, estimate Plackett-Luce ranking models, and evaluate their predictive performance on held-out assortments. Combining these estimates with synthetic customer preferences, we find that accounting for AI mediation can materially change optimal assortments and revenue. Across the tested capacity configurations, ignoring mediation yields mean revenue losses between 2.52% and 11.37% relative to the PL optimum. A much simpler deterministic plug-in, based only on the ordering of fitted AI utilities, performs substantially better, with mean losses of at most 0.53%. Motivated by this performance, we study assortment optimization under deterministic mediation. We characterize its computational complexity and show that, for any fixed number of customer segments, the problem admits a fully polynomial-time approximation scheme.

entry.title: Robust Halo Orbit Stationkeeping Under Missed Thrust Events and Maneuver Execution Errors
entry.summary: Spacecraft stationkeeping is subject to various operational uncertainties such as missed thrust events, maneuver execution errors, and dynamics modeling errors. Missed thrust events are the most disruptive of these, and current practices mitigate that risk through Monte Carlo-driven heuristics and conservative margins that offer no formal safety guarantees and do not scale to multiple missed thrust events. This paper models these unplanned thruster outages through the Markov Jump System framework, and represents maneuver execution errors and dynamics linearization errors as bounded multiplicative noise. The resulting closed-loop system is a linear time-varying periodic Markov jump system with multiplicative noise, for which Lyapunov-like mean square stability and periodic set invariance conditions are derived. A linear matrix inequality-based optimal controller synthesis framework then designs a periodic, mode-dependent mean-square stable feedback policy that respects path constraints with probability one. The framework is demonstrated on the Earth-Moon 9:2 near-rectilinear halo orbit (NRHO), under both impulsive and low-thrust propulsion, and on a Saturn-Enceladus $L_1$ NRHO using impulsive propulsion. Nonlinear Monte Carlo simulations show that the spacecraft recovers from an arbitrary number of missed thrust events while respecting path constraints, and that the multiplicative noise model introduces additional robustness to maneuver execution error and linearization error.

entry.title: When Solvers Get Moody: Quantifying and Predicting Performance Variability in Mixed Integer Programming
entry.summary: Mixed-integer programming (MIP) solvers are widely used, yet their performance can vary substantially even under seemingly neutral perturbations. Such variability complicates benchmarking, and the interpretation of computational studies. We introduce the Weighted Variability Score (WVS), a robust multi-component metric that aggregates dispersion in normalized runtime, final optimality gap, LP iterations, and branch-and-bound nodes across repeated runs. On a large subset of MIPLIB 2017 instances, each solved in 100 randomized runs under a four-hour limit, WVS reveals a right-skewed distribution with a substantial upper tail: many instances are essentially stable, but some exhibit large variability that is not explained by basic properties alone. Notably, this experiment proved optimality for the open instance 'neos-5045105-creuse' in two SCIP runs. Using static descriptors and root-level features, a tree-based predictor with a gated tail uplift achieves a mean absolute error of 0.058 and Spearman rank correlation of 0.65 on a sealed test split. Feature-importance analysis highlights root degeneracy, matrix structure, coefficient ranges, and presolve reductions as the main drivers of high WVS. Because variability is systematic and partially predictable from inexpensive early-run features, our findings offer a practical tool for preemptive tuning and lay a foundation for fairer evaluation of new algorithms.
entry.arxiv:comment: 21 pages, including a 3-page electronic companion. An earlier conference version appeared in the IOS 2026 proceedings. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19478202

entry.title: Nonsmooth Optimization via Orthogonalized Momentum
entry.summary: Modern real application problems involve matrix-valued parameters, yet conventional optimizers treat them as vectors, thereby motivating matrix-aware methods that exploit input-output geometry, such as Muon which orthogonalizes the momentum matrices before parameter updates. Its empirical success raises a conceptual question: can orthogonalized momentum remain effective beyond smooth optimization? This paper studies this question for locally Lipschitz functions using a generalized derivative framework compatible with backpropagation.
